title: [P2] Hardening: isolate experimental/unverified HID protocol bits behind flags/modules
description:
Several protocol offsets/mappings are explicitly marked as "needs verification" or "experimental" but live alongside trusted parsing code.

Refs:
- `Sources/JamCon/ButtonMapping.swift:112`
- `Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift:544` (output reports)
- `Sources/JamCon/G502XHIDProtocol.swift:1`

Separate experimental paths behind a feature flag / debug-only module and document which constants are trusted for production behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unverified/experimental protocol code is isolated (debug-only or feature-flagged)
- Production parsing uses only documented/trusted offsets
- Documentation clearly states what is verified vs speculative

title: [P1] KeyCaptureManager: fix event tap Unmanaged return semantics (avoid retain/leak)
description:
`KeyCaptureManager.installEventTap` returns `Unmanaged.passRetained(event)` from the CGEventTap callback in several paths. Typical event tap callbacks return `passUnretained` for events they pass through; retaining can leak events over time.

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/KeyCaptureManager.swift:77`.

Audit all callback return paths and ensure the correct ownership model is used.
acceptance_criteria:
- Event tap callback returns correct Unmanaged ownership (`passUnretained` when passing events through)
- No functional regression in key capture behavior (keyDown + flagsChanged handling)
- No observable event leak during prolonged capture sessions

title: [P2] UX: show captured keys using current keyboard layout (not hardcoded keycodes)
description:
`KeyCombo.displayName` uses a hardcoded keycode→label mapping that is mostly US-layout and incomplete.

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/ButtonAction.swift:68`.

Use the current keyboard layout to render key names (while keeping special keys/arrow keys correct) so the UI matches what the user actually pressed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Displayed key names match the active keyboard layout for normal keys
- Special keys (arrows, Return, Escape, etc.) still render correctly
- Captured key combos remain stable in storage (still keyed by keyCode+modifiers)

title: Batch HID lock snapshot in AppState report callback
description: onReportData currently grabs OSAllocatedUnfairLock repeatedly via cachedIsLeftController, cachedIsEnabled, cachedJoystickScrollEnabled/Speed/Acceleration, and trigger threshold. Acquire the lock once, capture all needed cached values (plus pause flag if feasible), and use that snapshot for the entire HID report processing path. Goal: minimize per-report lock/unlock churn on the ~60–66 Hz hot path without changing behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- onReportData performs at most one lock acquisition for cached values per report (excluding unavoidable pause check) and uses a snapshot for subsequent logic
- Gyro, joystick scroll, and button processing behave identically (no regression in modes or enable/disable behavior)
- Measured or reasoned lock/unlock count per report is reduced vs current implementation

title: [P2] Cleanup: remove or adopt unused UIStateStore
description:
`UIStateStore` exists but is not referenced anywhere in the project.

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/Utilities/UIStateStore.swift:4`.

Decide whether to delete it or integrate it into the current architecture (AppState/SettingsStore/InputEngine).
acceptance_criteria:
- `UIStateStore` is either deleted or used in production code
- No unused/duplicate state bridges remain

title: Swap NSLock to OSAllocatedUnfairLock in hot paths
description: AppState uses NSLock for cached flags accessed from HID callbacks. Replace with OSAllocatedUnfairLock (or os_unfair_lock) for lower overhead and to match GyroSettings’ locking approach. Keep the API surface the same while reducing lock latency on the input thread.

title: Make settings tabs type-aware (Controller, Buttons, Mouse/Stick) for Joy-Con
description: Update Controller/Buttons/Mouse/Stick tabs to switch content based on controller type: Joy-Con gets its own button list (including the extra four buttons) and stick controls; PSVR2 keeps its current UI. Ensure the tabs read/write the correct stored profile per type and show a Joy-Con-specific selector in the Controller tab. For now, focus on UI/plumbing, not full action execution.

title: Reuse debug buffers to reduce allocations when debug is on
description: When debug rendering is active, reuse preallocated buffers/arrays for pending byte/bit changes and report copies instead of rebuilding them each report. Clear by count instead of reallocating to keep the HID path lean even while debugging.

comments.author: jturnshek
comments.text: Closed in error; debug buffer reuse not implemented yet.

title: [P0] Sense: fix device timestamp capture regression (duplicate check clears valid timestamps)
description:
`SenseController.handleInputValue` currently assigns `lastDeviceTicks = ts` and then immediately checks `if (lastDeviceTicks ?? 0) == ts { lastDeviceTimestamp = nil; return }`, which will always be true and clears valid device timestamps.

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift:524` (see especially the logic around `Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift:539`).

Impact: Sense gyro uses host timestamps instead of device timestamps, increasing dt jitter and degrading filtering/accel behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- `lastDeviceTimestamp` updates on non-duplicate IOHID timestamps
- Duplicate ticks clear/ignore device timestamps without clearing valid ones
- Sense `effectiveTimestamp` in `handleInputReport` uses device time when available (`Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift:490`)

title: [P0] Thread-safety: radial menu cursor tracking reads engine state across threads
description:
Mouse radial menu cursor polling uses a `DispatchSourceTimer` on the main queue that reads/writes engine state (`radialMenuOwnerKind`, `mouseMode.radialMenuButtonHeld`, `radialMenuCursorAnchor`, `radialMenuAccumulator`) while the HID thread mutates mode state.

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:1106`.

This needs explicit synchronization/ownership (e.g. engine queue + main-only UI callback) to avoid races and inconsistent selection.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cursor polling and radial menu state updates are synchronized with mode-state mutations
- No shared radial-menu state is read/written concurrently from main + HID threads
- Selection remains correct under load and on rapid press/release
notes: Synchronizing mouse radial menu cursor polling with engineQueue (no main-queue timer mutating engine state) and removing NSEvent usage from the poll loop.

title: Add controller-type aware selection and persistence
description: Extend controller discovery/selection to handle both PSVR2 and Joy-Con: unify ControllerInfo with type/side, maintain separate last-selected IDs per type, and allow selecting a single Joy-Con as the active device (PSVR2 can still be selected). Ensure connection change callbacks and AppState track the active controller type for downstream UI/state.

title: Retune One Euro filter and dt handling for 200Hz Joy-Con gyro feed
description: Joy-Con delivers ~200Hz bundled gyro samples but InputProcessor assumes ~66Hz: fallbackRate is forced to 66Hz and expectedDt is 1/66s. This makes the One Euro filter overly aggressive and stall detection too lax. Update the hot path to use a ~200Hz cadence (fallbackRate ~= 200, expectedDt ~= 1/200, matching stall reset threshold) and adjust default minCutoff/beta so the smoothing feel matches PSVR2 at its 60Hz rate. Ensure filter reset still occurs on true stalls and no lag is introduced during fast motion.
acceptance_criteria:
- OneEuroFilter fallbackRate uses the actual ~200Hz Joy-Con cadence; expectedDt in processGyro reflects 1/200s with an appropriate stall clamp
- Default filter settings are retuned for 200Hz so perceived smoothing/latency matches PSVR2 behavior (no added lag compared to current PSVR2 feel)
- Bluetooth stalls still reset the filters correctly; no regressions in cursor stability at rest or during fast flicks

title: Extend Debug tab to display Joy-Con reports/bytes
description: Adapt DebugTab to handle Joy-Con: switch report length/offset metadata based on active controller type, render the byte grid with change highlighting for Joy-Con report length, and surface minimal Joy-Con button/stick/IMU readouts. Keep PSVR2 debug behavior unchanged when PSVR2 is active.

title: [P0] Thread-safety: controller discovery + connection snapshots (Sense/JoyCon/G502X)
description:
Controller discovery lists and connection flags are mutated on HID threads but read from UI/main via `InputEngine.availableControllers`, `InputEngine.isConnected`, and `AppState.refreshControllerList()`.

Key refs:
- `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:289`
- `Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift:48`
- `Sources/JamCon/JoyConHIDController.swift:85`
- `Sources/JamCon/G502XHIDController.swift:159`

This needs a thread-safe snapshot API (lock/actor/queue confinement) so UI never reads mutable HID-thread state directly.
acceptance_criteria:
- UI-facing controller lists are produced from a thread-safe snapshot (no direct read of HID-thread-mutated arrays)
- Connection state (`isConnected`, selected IDs/names) is safe to read from main
- TSAN (or equivalent reasoning) shows no races in controller list/connection state paths
notes: Implementing thread-safe snapshot APIs for discovered controllers/mice + connection state; update InputEngine/AppState to use snapshots.

title: Instrument HID→CGEvent latency for Joy-Con gyro path
description: We need hard numbers on where latency accrues. Add optional diagnostics that timestamp at key points: (1) IOHIDValue callback arrival, (2) after decoding, (3) before/after processGyro, (4) before CGEvent post. Emit lightweight logs/counters (guarded behind a debug flag) so we can measure average/max latency and stalls without spamming production builds.
acceptance_criteria:
- Debug mode captures timestamps at HID callback, post-decode, pre/post processGyro, and pre-CGEvent post, computing deltas without significant overhead when enabled
- Diagnostics are gated (off by default) and safe to leave in production builds
- Documentation or log output shows how to enable and collect the latency measurements, and demonstrates end-to-end timing with Joy-Con

title: Reduce Date() calls in radial menu trail update
description: Pass a single timestamp through radial menu trail update/pruning to avoid multiple Date() allocations per gyro update when radial menu is active.

title: Strengthen dt fallback and diagnostics
description: Keep using device timestamps, but add guards for nil/duplicate device ts (fallback to host time) and log/diagnose when dt hits clamp thresholds frequently. Aim is to make jitter handling more robust and observable without changing core behavior.

title: [P2] Cleanup: remove unused ButtonStateTracker
description:
`ButtonStateTracker` is defined but not used anywhere. It duplicates button edge-detection that InputEngine already implements with array-backed state.

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/ButtonMapping.swift:174`.

Remove it or repurpose it (e.g., debug-only utilities) to reduce maintenance surface area.
acceptance_criteria:
- `ButtonStateTracker` is removed or used intentionally
- No dead code remains in `Sources/JamCon/ButtonMapping.swift`

title: [P0] CrashReporter: make signal handling async-signal-safe
description:
`CrashReporter.handleSignal` runs inside a POSIX signal handler but uses Foundation and other non-async-signal-safe APIs (Date formatting, Thread.callStackSymbols, FileManager/file I/O).

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/CrashReporter.swift:50`.

This is undefined behavior and can deadlock/hang (especially if the crash occurred while holding an internal lock).
acceptance_criteria:
- Signal handler path uses only async-signal-safe primitives (e.g., pre-opened fd + `write`, atomic flags)
- Any richer crash reporting (stack traces, formatting) is moved out of the signal handler (e.g., next launch, or rely on macOS crash logs)
- App termination behavior remains correct (re-raises signal or exits)

title: [P1] Concurrency: standardize controller callback dispatch (thread/queue contract)
description:
Callback threading is inconsistent across controllers (some dispatch to main, others call directly on the HID thread). This is easy to misuse and can create UI threading bugs.

Example: Joy-Con fires `onControllersChanged?()` on the HID thread (`Sources/JamCon/JoyConHIDController.swift:265`), while Sense/G502X dispatch some callbacks to `DispatchQueue.main`.

Define and enforce a single callback contract (e.g. all controller callbacks delivered on engine queue, with UI hops in AppState) and make all controllers comply.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each controller documents which thread/queue callbacks run on
- Implementation matches the contract for all callbacks (controllers changed, connection changed, report data, debug messages)
- AppState/UI code no longer needs to defensively hop threads except where required by the contract

title: [P2] Perf: debounce/batch settings persistence (avoid per-slider UserDefaults writes)
description:
Most gyro-related `@Published` properties in `AppState` call `saveGyroSettings()` on every value change, which writes to UserDefaults each time (e.g. while dragging sliders).

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/AppState.swift:508`.

Batch/debounce persistence so the engine still receives immediate updates via `SettingsStore.update`, but disk/UserDefaults writes happen at a reasonable cadence (or on explicit commit).
acceptance_criteria:
- Engine settings update immediately as the UI changes
- UserDefaults persistence is debounced/batched (no write spam while dragging)
- No regression to settings reload/migration behavior

title: Cache gyro settings snapshot for HID hot path
description: Avoid per-report OSAllocatedUnfairLock read of gyroSettings in AppState.onReportData by maintaining a cached settings snapshot updated on change, so HID processing uses a lock-free struct (similar to other cached values).

title: Debounce disk writes for sliders (gyro, radial, mappings) to remove laggy drags
description:
Observed: slider didSets call persistence on every tick (e.g., `gyroSettings.save()` inside AppState gyro properties; `UserDefaults` writes in joystick/radial sliders; radial menu config JSON saved on every change). Dragging sliders drives synchronous disk I/O on the main thread, contributing to UI stutter.
Proposal:
- Switch sliders to update in-memory state during drag and persist on `onEditingChanged == false` or via a short debounce (e.g., DispatchWorkItem) on the main queue.
- Keep live values for processing, but batch writes to `UserDefaults`/JSON to avoid per-tick file churn.
Files: Sources/PSVR2Gyro/AppState.swift (gyro @Published didSets, joystick scroll settings); Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Models/GyroSettings.swift (save); Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Models/RadialMenu.swift (save); Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Views/Settings/*.swift (sliders).
Goal: Slider drags feel responsive with no visible hitch from synchronous persistence.

title: Implement Joy-Con raw HID driver (PSVR2-style)
description: Add a Nintendo Joy-Con HID driver that mirrors PSVR2Controller: match vendor 0x057E and PIDs 0x2006/0x2007, probe type via SPI 0x6012, send subcommands to set input mode 0x30 and enable IMU, seize device, and stream raw input reports (define JoyConHIDProtocol with report length/offsets). Expose callbacks for report bytes + decoded gyro/accel, stick, and battery, using a reusable buffer and Mach timestamps similar to PSVR2.

title: Track cursor internally with periodic resync to reduce per-move mouseLocation calls
description: Maintain an internal cursor position in Cocoa coordinates and apply gyro dx/dy to it, posting CGEvents without calling NSEvent.mouseLocation every move. Resync from the system cursor on startup, screen changes, after drags/warps, or on a low-rate timer to handle external cursor moves. Ensure clamping stays correct and coordinate spaces remain consistent. Goal: remove per-move mouseLocation lookup while keeping cursor behavior stable.

title: [P2] Observability: unify logging (os.Logger + DebugBuffer mirror) and rate-limit hot-path logs
description:
Logging is currently a mix of `print` and `DebugBuffer.log`, with some logs happening on hot paths. Standardize on `os.Logger` for structured logs, and optionally mirror to `DebugBuffer` for in-app log viewing.

Refs:
- `Sources/JamCon/Engine/DebugBuffer.swift:256`
- `Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift:141`
- `Sources/JamCon/JoyConHIDController.swift:521`
- `Sources/JamCon/G502XHIDController.swift:307`

Also ensure hot-path debug logs are gated/rate-limited to avoid performance regressions.
acceptance_criteria:
- All non-user-facing logging goes through a consistent logging facade
- In-app log tab still works (via DebugBuffer mirror or similar)
- Hot-path logging is gated/rate-limited (no per-frame spam in release behavior)

title: Coalesce radial menu updates to avoid per-report Task creation
description: When gyro mode is .radialMenu, onReportData spawns a new Task {@MainActor} for every HID report, which can queue up if the main actor lags. Introduce coalescing (e.g., store latest delta and drive a single main-actor updater) to keep UI current without spawning one task per sample.
acceptance_criteria:
- Radial menu gyro updates no longer create an unbounded Task per report; updates are coalesced or limited to one in-flight
- UI responsiveness for radial selection remains correct (no dropped highlights/selection errors)
- No accumulation of pending Tasks on the main actor under load

title: Run HID manager on dedicated high-QoS run loop
description: Currently IOHIDManager is scheduled on the main CFRunLoop (see PSVR2Controller.start), so SwiftUI/UI work can delay HID report handling, inflating dt and adding jitter. Move HID scheduling to a dedicated high-priority thread/run loop for input processing and only dispatch UI updates back to the main actor. This should reduce latency spikes and stutter in gyro-driven mouse movement.

title: [P0] Thread-safety: remove AppKit usage from non-main engine paths
description:
Several "World 1" / engine-side paths call AppKit APIs from non-main threads, which is not thread-safe and can cause intermittent crashes or UI glitches.

Key refs:
- `NSEvent.mouseLocation` used from engine (`Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:630`, `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:1116`)
- `NSScreen.screens` / `NotificationCenter` observers in `MouseController` while engine calls into it (`Sources/JamCon/MouseController.swift:32`, `Sources/JamCon/MouseController.swift:245`)
- `NSWorkspace.shared` used in system actions (`Sources/JamCon/ActionExecutor.swift:129`)

Fix by confining AppKit calls to `@MainActor` and/or replacing with CoreGraphics-safe equivalents in the engine thread.
acceptance_criteria:
- AppKit APIs are only called on the main actor
- Engine/hot-path uses only thread-safe/CoreGraphics primitives
- No regressions to cursor movement, clicks, scroll, radial menu positioning, or system actions
notes: Removing AppKit calls from engine paths by switching cursor/screen queries to CoreGraphics, and dispatching any remaining AppKit work (e.g., NSWorkspace/media keys) to the main actor.

title: Use real HID timestamps for bundled Joy-Con samples instead of clamped spacing
description: JoyConSwift backfills per-sample timestamps by dividing the packet delta by 3 and clamping spacing to 1/200–1/2000s. If a packet is late, downstream code still thinks samples were spaced 5ms apart, masking stalls and skewing dt. Relax or remove the clamp and propagate the true Mach-based timestamps so InputProcessor can see real gaps and reset filters appropriately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Per-sample timestamps reflect actual Mach ticks (no fixed 5ms clamp when packets are late); sample spacing is derived from real packet deltas
- InputProcessor receives monotonic timestamps that never go backward and handles stalls correctly (filters reset on real gaps)
- No regressions in gyro processing stability; dt remains within a sensible bound to avoid divide-by-small errors

title: Gate debug byte/bit tracking and reuse report buffers
description: Per-report debug bookkeeping runs even when not viewing the debug tab: full 78-byte copies, byte/bit change tracking, and Date allocations. Add a flag to skip this work when debug rendering is off and reuse preallocated buffers to reduce allocations and comparisons on the HID thread.

title: Deburst bundled Joy-Con samples so CGEvents aren’t posted in 66Hz bursts
description: Each Joy-Con HID packet contains 3 gyro samples but sensorHandler fires them back-to-back, so mouse moves post in 66Hz bursts rather than ~200Hz spacing. Evaluate and implement a low-latency strategy: either process only the newest sample per packet (for latency parity with PSVR2) or spread the 3 samples over ~5ms intervals without adding noticeable lag. Goal: smoother, more responsive cursor updates instead of clumped bursts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hot path no longer posts all three sample deltas at once each packet; either single-sample or time-sliced delivery is implemented and selectable if needed
- End-user cursor motion feels smoother (no bursty micro-stutter) and latency does not increase relative to current behavior
- No regression in clutch/scroll/zoom modes; sampling strategy applies consistently across modes

title: Reduce Joy-Con gyro hot-path overhead (raw Int16 + single settings snapshot)
description: On each gyro sample we allocate GyroData, convert Float→Double, and read many InputSettings fields individually (multiple lock hits). Introduce a raw Int16 + timestamp path from JoyConSwift into InputProcessor (matching PSVR2), and add a single InputSettings snapshot for gyro processing to cut per-sample locking. Objective: lower CPU/latency on the HID thread without changing behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Gyro processing can consume raw Int16 values + timestamp directly (or uses a zero-allocation struct) without Float→Double conversions on the hot path
- InputProcessor receives a single settings snapshot per gyro dispatch instead of multiple lock acquisitions
- Behavior (sensitivity, mapping, filtering) matches current output; no regressions in clutch/scroll/zoom or activity detection

title: Apply button/mode state before gyro movement per report
description: Currently onGyroData runs before onReportData updates button states and gyro mode, so drag/scroll/clutch toggles apply one packet late. Reorder processing so button/joystick decoding and mode selection happen for the same HID report before applying gyro deltas, eliminating a frame of latency when switching modes.

title: Reuse HID report buffer and avoid double gyro/accel decoding
description: handleInputReport allocates a new [UInt8] per report and decodes gyro/accel, then AppState decodes gyro/accel again. Reuse a persistent buffer (or pointer) for the report bytes, and pass the already-decoded IMU values/timestamp to AppState to eliminate the extra allocation and double decode.
acceptance_criteria:
- No per-report heap allocation for the 78-byte input report (buffer is reused)
- AppState consumes pre-decoded gyro/accel/timestamp without re-decoding the same bytes
- IMU/gyro processing and debug views still receive correct data

title: Investigate PSVR2 Sense Circle/Square triggering unwanted system actions (Escape-like) on macOS Tahoe 26.1
description:
On macOS Tahoe 26.1, PSVR2 Sense controllers connected over Bluetooth cause at least the Circle button (and possibly Square) to trigger unwanted behavior in other apps (e.g., closing popup windows / Escape-like cancel) in addition to JamCon receiving the button via raw HID.

Current hypothesis: macOS GameController stack (`/usr/libexec/gamecontrollerd` + related services) is handling certain controller buttons at the system level (similar to the already-known PlayStation/Home button opening Launchpad/Arcade) and this path may run in parallel with IOHID report delivery.

Repo evidence:
- `Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift` opens Sense devices with `kIOHIDOptionsTypeSeizeDevice` both on discovery and activation.
- `docs/Sense-HID-Protocol.md` notes the PlayStation button triggers Apple Arcade/Launchpad at the system level.
- `Sources/JamCon/Views/Settings/ButtonsTab.swift` warns Square/Circle may trigger unwanted keyboard shortcuts.
- `/System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.GameController.gamecontrollerd.plist` auto-launches on IOHIDDevice matches for Generic Desktop usages 0x04/0x05 and publishes `com.apple.GameController.system-button-service`.

Unknowns:
- Is Circle/Square producing a real keyboard event (e.g., keycode 53 Escape) or a higher-level cancel/back action that never becomes a keypress?
- Is the behavior configurable via System Settings → Game Controllers (profiles/remapping), or is it hard-coded for this device class?

Notes / constraints observed in this environment:
- `hidutil` on this system exposes `list`, `dump`, `property`; no `eventmonitor` subcommand.
- `hidutil dump` currently reports `ClientRecords/ServiceRecords Unavailable`.

Repro sketch:
1) Pair PSVR2 Sense controllers over Bluetooth.
2) Start JamCon (IOHID reads button bits normally).
3) In another app, open a dialog/popup; press Circle; popup closes (Escape-like).
design:
Proposed investigation steps:
1) Use `hidutil list --matching '{"VendorID":0x054c}'` while Sense is connected; check if any service appears with `PrimaryUsagePage=0x07` (Keyboard) or `0x0C` (Consumer). If present, Circle may be coming from a separate HID keyboard/consumer interface.
2) Use a system event viewer to confirm event type:
   - Karabiner-Elements EventViewer (if available) to see keycode 53/other.
   - Or add an optional JamCon debug-only monitor using a listen-only `CGEventTap` / `NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents` to log last ~N keyDown/keyUp/systemDefined events, including keycode/modifiers and (if possible) event source PID.
3) Try System Settings → Game Controllers profile/remapping for the Sense controller; see if Circle/Square behavior changes.
4) Based on findings:
   - If it’s a real key event: consider per-device mapping/blocking (hidutil/Karabiner) or app-time CGEventTap suppression while JamCon is active.
   - If it’s a higher-level system action: focus on Game Controllers settings/profile controls; disabling `gamecontrollerd` is last resort due to system-wide impact.

Do not disable `gamecontrollerd` by default; treat as fallback only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Determine whether Circle/Square generates actual keyboard events (keycode/modifiers) vs a non-keyboard system action.
- Identify the source path (e.g., controller exposes a keyboard HID service vs events injected by `gamecontrollerd`).
- Document a recommended mitigation for macOS 26.1 (prefer System Settings remap; otherwise per-device key blocking/suppression).
- If needed, propose/implement a JamCon debug aid to surface the evidence (e.g., optional system event monitor showing recent keyDown/keyUp + source PID).

title: Reduce radial menu trail allocations and tighten angle normalization
description: TrailPoint currently allocates a UUID and Date per point, and angle normalization uses while loops. Replace UUID with a lightweight incrementing ID, reuse a single timestamp per update, keep trail capacity between updates, and switch angle normalization to fmod-based clamping. Preserve visual behavior and lifetime limits.
acceptance_criteria:
- Trail point creation avoids UUID() and reuses a timestamp per update; removeAll uses keepingCapacity where appropriate
- Angle normalization uses fmod (or equivalent bounded math) instead of unbounded while loops
- Radial menu trail visuals and selection behavior remain unchanged (maxTrailPoints and lifetime respected)

title: [P2] Refactor: split oversized files into focused modules
description:
Several files are very large, increasing change risk and making ownership boundaries unclear (InputEngine, G502XHIDController, AppState, DebugTab).

Refs:
- `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift`
- `Sources/JamCon/G502XHIDController.swift`
- `Sources/JamCon/AppState.swift`
- `Sources/JamCon/Views/Settings/DebugTab.swift`

Split by responsibility (e.g. per-controller processors, button handling, radial menu routing, debug UI sections) without changing behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Target files are split into smaller, coherent units with minimal public surface
- No behavior change (verified by manual sanity + existing debug tools)
- Ownership boundaries (Engine vs UI vs HID parsing) are clearer

title: Optimize radial menu rendering (static layers + lightweight cursor/highlight)
description:
Observed: `RadialMenuState` publishes `ghostPosition`/highlight indexes and `RadialMenuView` rebuilds all pie slices, labels, glass effects every cursor move. Trig/layout runs per-frame, and highlight changes force full view recomposition.
Proposal:
- Split static geometry (inner/outer ring slices + labels) into a pre-rendered layer/Canvas or an `EquatableView` keyed by `RadialMenuConfiguration`, and keep a minimal overlay for ghost cursor/highlight.
- Reduce per-delta main-thread churn: replace per-report `Task { @MainActor ... }` in `AppState` radial path with a throttled main queue hop or dedicated actor; consider trimming trail computations to avoid new Dates in the view.
Files: Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Views/RadialMenuView.swift; Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Models/RadialMenuState.swift; Sources/PSVR2Gyro/AppState.swift (radial menu update scheduling).
Goal: Radial menu and ghost cursor stay smooth at 60–120 Hz without re-rendering all slices on each move.
notes: Implemented engine-side radial menu UI throttling/coalescing to ~120Hz: `InputEngine` now accumulates `radialMenuPendingDelta` on the hot path and flushes via a DispatchSource timer instead of calling `onRadialMenuUpdate` per gyro sample; also bumped mouse radial-menu cursor polling to ~120Hz and ensured timers/overlay are cancelled on `stop()`/`deselectController()`. Built successfully with `xcodebuild -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`.

title: Trim per-report allocations in AppState hot path
description: Minor hot-path cleanups: reuse/cached PSVR2ButtonMapping for left/right, avoid creating the byteAt closure per report, and only call Date()/debug tracking when debug rendering is active.
acceptance_criteria:
- No per-report allocation of PSVR2ButtonMapping or byteAt closure in onReportData
- Date() and debug tracking work are skipped entirely when debug rendering is disabled
- Functional behavior for mapping, debug bytes/bits, and UI updates remains unchanged

title: Hook Joy-Con reports into AppState and type-specific storage
description: Wire the new Joy-Con driver into AppState: route onReportData/onConnectionChange into existing throttling, resize report buffers to Joy-Con length when active, and add a Joy-Con-specific button mapping profile + settings store (shared across Joy-Cons) without affecting PSVR2 profiles. Maintain type-aware cached values so downstream processing can branch without crashes when the report length/offsets differ.

title: Replace button state dictionaries with fixed-size storage on HID path
description: processButtonActions and buttonStates use Dictionary<LogicalButton,Bool> and look up mappings via string keys, adding hashing overhead each report. Replace with array/bitset keyed by an integer-backed enum to remove per-frame dictionary costs while preserving semantics (press/release edge detection, holds, and exported buttonStates for UI/debug).
acceptance_criteria:
- Button state tracking on the HID thread no longer uses Dictionary lookups per button
- Edge detection, hold timers, and buttonStates exposure still function correctly
- LogicalButton can be indexed deterministically (e.g., stable ordering) to back the fixed-size storage

title: Use circular buffer for gyro bias samples
description: GyroProcessor.updateBias appends samples and trims with removeFirst(), adding O(n) churn in the bias buffer. Replace with a fixed-size ring buffer to keep bias updates O(1) and avoid allocations while collecting stationary samples.

title: GyroProcessor math/alloc optimizations and OneEuro constant
description: Tighten GyroProcessor hot path: preallocate bias buffer up front, maintain running sums to avoid per-sample reduce, reuse a single speed/sqrt result across acceleration/adaptive beta, and hoist 2π to a static constant in OneEuroFilter. Also skip gyro/accel decoding when callbacks are nil to avoid wasted work.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bias buffer is allocated once (not lazily on first stationary frame) and bias updates avoid O(n) reduce per sample by using a running sum/count
- Speed computation reused (no redundant sqrt) in adaptive smoothing/acceleration
- OneEuroFilter uses a cached 2π constant instead of recomputing each call
- Gyro/accel decoding in PSVR2Controller is skipped when corresponding callbacks are nil
- No behavior regressions in calibration, filtering, or cursor feel

title: [P1] SenseController: ensure onReportData bytes are a stable snapshot (no live buffer exposure)
description:
`SenseController` reuses `reportBuffer` for IOHID callbacks and then passes that `[UInt8]` outward via `onReportData`, which risks sharing storage with a live callback buffer and is easy to break via copy-on-write.

Ref: `Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift:500`.

G502X already documents a similar crash risk when sharing storage with callback buffers (`Sources/JamCon/G502XHIDController.swift:255`). Ensure Sense report bytes passed to consumers are stable and cannot invalidate the pointer registered with IOHID.
acceptance_criteria:
- `onReportData` receives a snapshot whose storage is independent of the IOHID callback buffer
- No copy-on-write of the registered report buffer can occur due to downstream consumers
- Debug views and InputEngine processing still see correct bytes/length

title: Simplify joystick scroll math and gating
description: Trim per-report math in joystick scroll: consider a lighter-weight acceleration or power curve, and ensure the path is fully gated when not in use. Goal: reduce computation on the HID thread for joystick scroll users while keeping feel acceptable.

title: [P0] Thread-safety: make MouseController state concurrency-safe
description:
`MouseController` maintains mutable state (`cachedPosition`, `cachedBounds`, `cursorHideCount`, timers/observers) that is mutated from AppKit notifications/timers and also from engine calls (often off-main). There is no synchronization.

Refs:
- `Sources/JamCon/MouseController.swift:45`
- `Sources/JamCon/MouseController.swift:245`
- `Sources/JamCon/MouseController.swift:269`

Make `MouseController` single-threaded (main actor or dedicated serial queue) or protect all mutable state with a lock, and ensure callers respect the contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- No data races in MouseController mutable state under TSAN (or equivalent reasoning)
- Cursor movement/click/scroll remain responsive at HID rates
- Cursor hide/show balancing remains correct across multiple modes

title: [P0] Thread-safety: serialize hold timers with report processing (InputEngine)
description:
Hold detection uses `holdQueue.asyncAfter` to fire a `DispatchWorkItem` that mutates `buttonPressStates` and executes actions while the HID callback thread is also mutating button state arrays.

Refs:
- `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:40`
- `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:832`

This is a data race and can cause missed/double actions or corrupt state. Hold timers should execute on the same serialized context as report processing (engine queue) or protect shared state with a lock and clear invariants.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hold timers do not mutate shared button state concurrently with report processing
- Hold actions fire exactly once per press when configured
- TSAN (or equivalent reasoning) shows no races in hold-related state
notes: Starting fix: remove holdQueue/HID-thread data races by serializing hold-timer execution with report processing (likely via an engine serial queue) and ensuring hold actions fire exactly once per press.

title: Cache drag/scroll/radial mapping flags instead of per-frame scans
description: currentGyroMode calls buttonMappingProfile.hasDragMapping (and similar) which scans the mappings dictionary each frame on the HID hot path. Cache booleans for hasDragMapping/hasScrollMapping/hasRadialMenuMapping whenever the profile is loaded or mutated, and use those cached values in currentGyroMode.
acceptance_criteria:
- hasDragMapping/hasScrollMapping/hasRadialMenuMapping are computed when the mapping profile changes, not each frame
- currentGyroMode uses cached flags and performs no dictionary scan on the hot path
- Behavior remains identical for mode selection when mappings are edited

title: Use device/driver timestamps for gyro dt
description: Gyro processing uses host arrival time (CACurrentMediaTime) from IOHIDDeviceRegisterInputReportCallback. Switch to an input value callback that exposes IOHIDValueGetTimeStamp (or otherwise decode a monotonic counter if present) so dt is based on device/driver time rather than run-loop jitter. Add dt clamping/high-gap reset logic to keep One Euro filter and acceleration stable.

title: [P1] Concurrency: confine select/open/close/register to controller HID threads
description:
Controller selection (`selectController`, `deselectController`, `activateController`, `IOHIDDeviceOpen/Close/Register...`) can be invoked from the main actor via `InputEngine.setDeviceManaged`, but each controller also has its own HID thread/runloop.

Refs:
- `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:211`
- `Sources/JamCon/SenseController.swift:283`
- `Sources/JamCon/JoyConHIDController.swift:287`
- `Sources/JamCon/G502XHIDController.swift:465`

Move these operations onto the appropriate controller HID runloop (e.g. `CFRunLoopPerformBlock`) so IOKit and controller-internal state are mutated on one thread.
acceptance_criteria:
- All IOHID open/close/register/unregister calls run on the owning controller’s HID thread
- Selection changes are serialized with device callbacks (no cross-thread mutation of controller state)
- No regressions to reconnect/auto-select behavior

title: [P3] Tests: add unit tests for pure logic (GyroProcessor, filters, calibration, radial selection)
description:
Add unit tests for deterministic, non-IOKit logic to reduce regressions during refactors:
- `GyroProcessor` dt clamping + stall reset behavior
- `OneEuroFilter` basic smoothing expectations
- Joy-Con stick calibration/deadzone normalization (`JoyConStickCalibration`, `JoyConButtonMapping.joystickPosition`)
- Radial menu selection math (engine selection based on accumulator)

Refs:
- `Sources/JamCon/GyroProcessor.swift`
- `Sources/JamCon/OneEuroFilter.swift`
- `Sources/JamCon/JoyConButtonMapping.swift`
- `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:905`
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests cover key edge cases (stall dt, duplicate timestamps, deadzone boundaries, selection thresholds)
- Tests run locally without requiring HID devices
- Refactors in these areas are protected by CI/local test runs

title: [P0] Concurrency hardening: define & enforce threading model
description:
Multiple components mutate/read shared state across the HID threads, main actor, and ad-hoc queues without a consistent ownership model, leading to data races and undefined behavior.

Key refs:
- InputEngine exposes `availableControllers` by reading controller `discovered*` arrays that are mutated on HID threads (`Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:289`).
- Hold timers mutate shared arrays on `holdQueue` while reports mutate them on the HID callback thread (`Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:40`, `Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:832`).
- AppKit used from non-main threads in "World 1" paths (`Sources/JamCon/Engine/InputEngine.swift:630`, `Sources/JamCon/ActionExecutor.swift:129`, `Sources/JamCon/MouseController.swift:32`).

This epic establishes a single, explicit model (e.g. dedicated engine serial queue, main-actor UI, per-controller HID thread confinement + snapshot APIs) and removes remaining races.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented threading/ownership policy exists (README/design note) for Engine/Controllers/UI
- All mutable shared state accessed across threads is either confined to one queue/actor or protected via locks with clear invariants
- The high-frequency input path no longer touches AppKit off-main
- Child issues under this epic are completed and TSAN (or equivalent reasoning) shows no remaining races in affected areas
notes: Progress: controller discovery snapshots (JC-7kh) + hold-timer races (JC-uhq) fixed; removed AppKit off-main in engine paths (JC-dh1) by using CoreGraphics cursor/screen APIs and main-actor dispatch for NSWorkspace/media keys; mouse radial-menu cursor polling is now serialized on engineQueue (JC-538).

title: Throttle debug publishes to avoid UI jank in settings tabs
description:
Observed: `AppState` publishes `lastGyro*`, `lastAccel*`, `reportCount`, `batteryLevel`, `debugRefreshTrigger`, etc. every ~30–60 fps from `setupReportCallback`, while all tabs observe the same `AppState`, causing TabView/ScrollView recomputation and sluggish scrolling/slider drags even when not on the Debug tab.
Proposal:
- Gate or move live telemetry (`lastGyro*`, `lastAccel*`, `reportCount`, `batteryLevel`, `debugRefreshTrigger`) behind the Debug tab (`activeTab == .debug && debugRenderingEnabled`) or isolate into a debug-only observable model.
- Keep connection/meta fields publishing, but stop frame-ticker publishes from invalidating non-debug UI.
Files: Sources/PSVR2Gyro/AppState.swift (setupReportCallback, published properties); Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Views/Settings/*.swift (Tabs/TabHeader observe AppState).
Goal: scrolling and slider drags in settings are smooth because they no longer get rebuilt at 30+ fps by debug telemetry.
notes: Started implementation to gate debug publishes and throttle battery updates to reduce UI churn.

title: Cache ButtonActions by LogicalButton index to avoid string hashing
description: Maintain an array of ButtonActions keyed by LogicalButton.index to eliminate per-event String dictionary lookups in button action processing; update the cache whenever the mapping profile changes.

title: Cache screen bounds and cursor lookup off the hot path
description: MouseController recalculates NSScreen.screens, unions bounds, and queries NSEvent.mouseLocation on every move. Cache screen geometry and cursor position using CGDisplay APIs, update on screen-change notifications, and keep the movement path free of AppKit calls to reduce stutter.

title: Stop re-instantiating radial menu preview state on tab recompute
description:
Observed: `RadialMenuTab` constructs a new `RadialMenuState` in `previewState` every body recompute. Because the tab observes `AppState`, unrelated publishes (e.g., connection or settings changes) rebuild the preview `RadialMenuView`, causing needless allocations and render work.
Proposal:
- Hold a `@StateObject`/cached preview state that only updates when `radialMenuConfiguration` changes, or derive a simple `View` that doesn’t recreate the state per recomposition.
Files: Sources/PSVR2Gyro/Views/Settings/RadialMenuTab.swift (menuPreview/previewState).
Goal: Radial tab stays responsive; preview does not churn when unrelated app state changes.
